title: Dodgers vs. Brewers Game 4: Expert Picks Predict Championship Sweep Threat – CBS Sports Preview
body:
The Milwaukee Brewers are poised to clinch the National League pennant on Thursday night, while the Los Angeles Dodgers face the prospect of a historic sweep in the 2026 NLCS. After three straight defeats, the defending champions must win Game 4 to stay alive, but the momentum in Milwaukee is palpable, and most analysts believe the Brewers have the upper hand to close out the series and advance to the World Series for the first time since 1982.

Milwaukee’s pitching staff has been the linchpin of the series, delivering three consecutive quality starts that have stifled the Dodgers’ potent offense. Starting right‑hander Colin Rea, who threw six scoreless innings in Game 3, is slated to take the mound again, backed by a bullpen anchored by veteran reliever Trevor Megill. The Brewers have limited Los Angeles to a .186 batting average over the first three games, a stark contrast to the .321 average they posted during the regular season. The ability to keep the Dodgers’ sluggers—Mookie Betts, Freddie Freeman and Cody Bellinger—from finding gaps will be the decisive factor.

Conversely, the Dodgers’ lineup, which has been the engine behind back‑to‑back championships, looks out of sync. In Game 1, they were held to a single run, and even the usually reliable Freddie Freeman has struggled, batting .167 in the series. Manager Dave Roberts has shuffled the order, inserting rookie outfielder Jace Jung in the leadoff spot in hopes of sparking a rally, but the adjustments have yet to translate into runs. The Dodgers’ bullpen, which was a cornerstone of their recent postseason success, has been exposed; a blown save in Game 2 and a shaky ninth inning in Game 3 have eroded confidence.

The broader narrative of the NLCS extends beyond the immediate matchup. Milwaukee entered the playoffs as a wild‑card team, yet they have outperformed expectations at every turn, defeating the Atlanta Braves and the San Diego Padres en route to the championship series. Their blend of veteran poise and youthful energy—highlighted by shortstop Willy Adames’s aggressive baserunning and outfielder William Contreras’s clutch hitting—has resonated with a city eager for a return to the World Series stage. In contrast, Los Angeles, despite a roster laden with All‑Stars, has shown signs of fatigue after a grueling regular season and a demanding postseason road.

If the Brewers secure the pennant, they will become the first NL team since the 2015 Royals’ league‑wide sweep to win a championship series without dropping a game. The victory would also mark a significant shift in the National League power balance, ending the Dodgers’ recent dominance and potentially ushering in a new era for the Brewers’ core group, which includes emerging talents like catcher James McCarthy and left‑handed pitcher Ben Brown. For the Dodgers, a loss would be a stark reminder that even the most decorated clubs can be undone by a combination of pitching excellence and timely hitting from an underdog opponent.

Looking ahead, Thursday’s game promises high stakes and intense drama. Should Milwaukee prevail, the city of Milwaukee will be preparing for its first World Series appearance in over four decades, while Los Angeles will be left to regroup and assess the future of a roster that, on paper, still boasts championship pedigree. Regardless of the outcome, Game 4 will serve as a defining moment in the 2026 postseason, illustrating how quickly fortunes can change in baseball’s unforgiving playoff landscape.
